body:
[aida:reviewer] RE-REVIEW SWEEP: NOTHING IS ACTIONABLE, AND I CAN NOW SAY THAT WITH A
POPULATION INSTEAD OF AN ASSERTION. Plus one write I made that you should know about.

I cross-referenced all 24 open PRs against their recorded verdicts and current heads:

    verdict at SAME head as the PR head    15    nothing reworked, nothing to re-review
    verdict with NO reviewed_sha            5    head movement undeterminable (BUG-1466/1467)
    no verdict at all                       3    #1989, #2019, #2042 - all held
    verdict at a MOVED head                 0    <- the re-review trigger; empty

So zero re-reviews are due. That is the same conclusion I have been reporting all
evening, but previously I was asserting it; this is the first time I have printed the
denominator. The 5 NO-SHA rows are the ones I cannot actually vouch for - a reworked
head would look identical to an unreworked one - and that is BUG-1466/BUG-1467's live
cost, not a separate problem.

ALL 24 OPEN PRs ARE HELD, AND EVERY HOLD HAS ATTRIBUTABLE REASON TEXT. I checked
because 24-of-24 looked like it might be a labelling defect - the gate's own comment
says a drain-mode PR is never labelled. It is not a defect: the mix is supervised-mode
auto-holds, your per-tick sweep holds, and my two reviewer holds. The convention is
holding.

WHAT I FOUND WHILE LOOKING, AND HAD ALREADY FILED WITHOUT REMEMBERING:

    label: synced     20
    label: unknown     4    PR-1989, PR-1998, PR-1999, PR-2006

All four "unknown" markers are yours - every one begins "advisor hold:". The gap
correlates exactly with the writer: markers placed via `aida merge-hold add` or the
drain carry the state line, markers written by the sweep do not. So the blind spot
concentrates in the holds a human reasoned about, which are the ones whose failure
matters most.

I checked all four against the forge: aida:merge-hold present on every one, all
BLOCKED. No live exposure. But the surface could not tell me that, which is the point -
a marker with no label renders identically, and in that case `merge-hold list` shows
the PR held while the required check is green and the PR is mergeable.

THIS IS TASK-1-170, WHICH I FILED AT 21:26 AND THEN REDISCOVERED AT 21:40 WITHOUT
RECOGNISING IT. I have added the measurement as a comment rather than filing again.
Worth noting as its own small data point: fourteen minutes was enough for me to lose
the filing. Searching before filing caught it; memory did not.

A WRITE I MADE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THE INTENT WAS WRONG EVEN THOUGH THE EFFECT WAS
SAFE. I ran `aida merge-hold list --fix` as a flag probe - I was checking whether --fix
existed after the BUG-1236 code comment mentioned it, and I ran it rather than reading
the help first. It re-synced all four markers. It is idempotent on the forge: the
labels were already present before and after, so nothing changed on GitHub, and it can
only ADD a label, never clear a hold. All 24 markers now read synced. No hold was
created, released or weakened.

The consequence you should know about: after that run, every row claims "synced" on the
marker's own authority - which is exactly the claim TASK-1-170 says cannot be trusted.
So --fix made the list MORE uniformly confident without making it more verified, and it
erased the one visible signal that four holds were unverified. If you were relying on
the unknown rows as a to-do marker, I have removed them. TASK-1-170's fix is unchanged
and now slightly more necessary.

NOTHING ELSE OUTSTANDING FROM ME. #2035 remains held on my refusal - clear only on my
re-review.
subject: Re-review sweep: 0 of 24 PRs have a moved head (15 same, 5 no-sha, 3 unverdicted) — and I ran merge-hold list --fix as a probe, which erased the 4 unknown-label rows
